intro: In the present, we make questions with do / does (lesson 6). In the past simple, there is one auxiliary for every person: did. The big trap: after did, the verb goes back to its base form. We say “Did you go?”, never “Did you went?”. This lesson also looks at negatives (didn't) and past questions with be (was / were).
objectifs: Make a yes/no question in the past: Did + subject + base form?
Ask Wh- questions: Where did you go? What did she say?
Give short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Not use did with be: Were you tired? Was it good?

sections.titre: Yes/no questions: Did + subject + base form
texte: To ask a question in the past simple, put did before the subject, then use the base form of the verb (no -ed, no irregular form): You visited Rome. → Did you visit Rome?
Did is the same for every person: Did I…? Did he…? Did they…? There is no “dids” and no special form for he / she / it.
Did carries the past. So the main verb must not be in the past: Did she buy (not “bought”) a new phone?

lignes: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Yes, she did. / No, she didn't.
Yes, they did. / No, they didn't.
Yes, it did. / No, it didn't.

exemples: Did they enjoy the concert? — Yes, they did.

texte: Add the question word (see lesson 29) at the start: Wh- + did + subject + base form? Where did you go? What did you eat? When did they arrive?
The word order is the same with How long, How much, What time…: How long did you stay? How much did it cost? What time did the film start?
Prepositions: in English they often go at the end of the question. Who did you go with? What did you talk about?
exemples: Where did you spend your holidays?
What time did you get up this morning?
Who did you meet at the party?
Who = the object (the person you met).

texte: Negatives work in the same way: subject + didn't (did not) + base form. I didn't see him. She didn't come.
Never put the verb in the past after didn't: “I didn't went” is wrong.
Negative questions show surprise: Didn't you like the film?
exemples: We didn't have time to eat.
have is a main verb here.

sections.titre: The exception: be in the past (was / were)
texte: With be, we do not use did. Just change the order of the subject and was / were (see lesson 39): You were tired. → Were you tired? It was expensive. → Was it expensive?
Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, it wasn't. Wh- questions: Where were you? How was your trip?
“How was…?” is very common to ask about someone's experience: How was the weekend? How was the exam?
exemples: How was your trip to Montréal?
Were you at the meeting? — No, I wasn't.

sections.titre: Short answers with did and didn't
texte: To answer a question with did, repeat did or didn't, not the main verb: Did you call her? — Yes, I did. (not “Yes, I called.”).
Just “Yes.” or “No.” is possible, but “Yes, I did.” is more polite and more natural.
To keep the conversation going, we often add some information: No, I didn't. I was too busy.
exemples: Did you lock the door? — Yes, I did.
Did the children eat everything? — No, they didn't. They weren't hungry.

formule: (Wh-) + did + subject + base form? · subject + didn't + base form · Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. · be: Was / Were + subject…?
prononciation: did is /dɪd/; in questions it is often weak and joins the pronoun: “Did you” ≈ /ˈdɪdʒu/ (“didja”).
“Did he” often becomes /ˈdɪdi/: the h disappears in fast speech.
didn't /ˈdɪdnt/: two syllables, the final t is very light.
Intonation: yes/no questions (Did you…?) usually go up at the end ↗; Wh- questions (Where did you…?) go down ↘.
In short answers, did is stressed: Yes, I DID.
erreurs: Did you went to the party?
Did you go to the party?
Where did you go last weekend?
You need the auxiliary did and question word order.
did carries the past, not like.
How was / were…? to ask about an experience.
Did you call him? — Yes, I called.
Preposition at the end in everyday English.

dialogue.contexte: On Monday morning, in an office in Yaoundé, Grâce asks her colleague Patrick about his weekend.
lignes: Morning, Patrick! How was your weekend?
Great, thanks. I went to Kribi with my brother.
Lucky you! How did you get there? Did you drive?
No, I didn't. We took the bus. It was cheaper.
In a small hotel near the beach. Did you do anything special?
do is the main verb here.
Not really. I stayed at home and watched a series.
Yes, it was. But I didn't finish it. I fell asleep!

mots: We stayed in a small hotel.
live in a place for a short time
Where did you spend your holidays?
a journey to a place and back
arrive at a place, travel to a place
I fell asleep in front of the TV.
a TV programme with many episodes
be too late for (a bus, train…)

exercices.consigne: Change each sentence into a question with did.
items: Did she buy a new car?

exercices.consigne: Ask the question for the part in CAPITALS.
items: What time did she arrive? / When did she arrive?
How much did the tickets cost?

exercices.consigne: Complete with Did, Was or Were.
Each sentence has one mistake. Correct it.
items: What did you do on Sunday?
Did you finish? — Yes, I finished.
Did you finish? — Yes, I did.

exercices.consigne: Write one question or sentence for each situation.
items: You want to know if your friend slept well last night.
Your friend went to the cinema. You want to know the person with him.
Who did you go to the cinema with?
Your friend went to a concert. You want her opinion.
Your sister read the question, but she doesn't know the answer. (understand)

exercices.consigne: Write five questions to ask a friend about last weekend (one yes/no question with did, three questions with Where / What / Who, and one with How was…?). Then answer two of them.
items: Did you go out on Saturday? Where did you go? What did you do there? Who did you go with? How was it? — Yes, I did. I went to a concert with my cousin. It was fantastic!

a_retenir: Questions: (Wh-) + did + subject + base form? (Did you go? Where did you go?)
Negatives: didn't + base form (I didn't see).
After did / didn't, never a past verb.
Short answers: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
With be, no did: Were you…? Was it…? How was…?
